why: I checked each PASS and FAIL condition against the words of its expect line. Checks 1, 2 and 4 hold. The cases in Check 1 are just examples of "limited to the range". Check 2 accepts any RangeError. Check 4's "# fail 0" matches what "passes" means. Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its PASS condition needs the script to print OK, and the script only finds a function if a markdown heading matches `^#+\s*name\s*\(`. The expect line only says README.md "documents every function math.js exports". A function documented in a bullet list, a table or plain prose would still meet those words but would fail this check. Requiring a heading format is stricter than the words, so it belongs under Advisory, not in the PASS condition.
